messages.author: e174d246020b1d33
messages.subject: help on using L-BFGS optimization
parts: I have been looking forward this new feature. The Rstan help file refers me to the manual, but there is no information in the current version (2.4.0) on the Stan homepage. I need some clarification on the optional parameters of the optimizing function, which have changed from Stan 2.3.0.

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] help on using L-BFGS optimization
parts:
Hi Eric,

Most of the optional parameters are exactly the same as for BFGS, in fact they're all detailed together in the manual.  The only one that's special for L-BFGS is the history_size parameter which specifies how many update vectors to keep around.  The default value of 5 is usually sensible but if you're seeing slow progress (lots of steps with alpha < 1) then you could try increasing this.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] help on using L-BFGS optimization
parts:
Sorry---I hadn't installed RStan 2.4 yet.

The doc is there for how to call it:

algorithm
One of "Newton", "BFGS", and "LBFGS" indicating which optimization algorithm is used. The default is BFGS.

and here are the parameters:



Other optional parameters.

• iter (integer), the maximum number of iterations

• save_iterations (logical), whether to save the iterations

• refresh (integer)

• init_alpha (double, default to 0.001), for BFGS and LBFGS, see manual of Stan

• tol_obj (double, default to 1e-12), for BFGS and LBFGS, see the manual of Stan

• tol_grad (double, default to 1e-8), for BFGS and LBFGS, see the manual of Stan

• tol_param (double, default to 1e-8), for BFGS and LBFGS, see the manual of Stan

• tol_rel_obj (double, default to 1e4), for BFGS and LBFGS, see the manual of Stan

• tol_rel_grad (double, default to 1e7), for BFGS and LBFGS, see the manual of Stan

• history_size (integer, default to 5), for LBFGS, see the manual of Stan

The manual reference should be to Stan, but we don't have that info in
the Stan manual yet --- it moved with other command doc to CmdStan, and we
need to pull it back out into the main manual for the next release. The link
to the CmdStan manual is:

http://mc-stan.org/cmdstan.html

More doc for L-BFGS is on p. 41.

The tolerances are absolute or relative for the objective function (log prob),
parameter distance, and gradient vector length. (Though it looks like
tol_rel_param is missing from the doc --- I don't know if it works or not in RStan.)

I also noted the CmdStan manual was not updated with the default being
LBFGS everywhere, but it is indeed the default now for CmdStan. I'll add a
to-do item for all of these for our manuals:

- update RStan to include all params in doc and make LBFGS the default

- update CmdStan manual to indicate LBFGS is the default

- update the Stan modeling language manual to explain the parameters
and have CmdStan manual just link to there

Sorry again for all the confusing doc.

- Bob
